title: Space-Time Electron Wave Packets with Tunable Skyrmion Textures
abstract: Space-Time Wave Packets (STWPs) have enabled numerous nontrivial properties, such as tunable group velocities, nondiffraction and nonlocal spin textures in optical fields. However, this has not been properly studied in matter waves. Here, we investigate free-electron STWPs, which are propagation-invariant and group-velocity-tunable matter wave packets, constructed by constraining the spatiotemporal spectrum of the electron wavefunction in momentum space. Due to the unique dispersion of free-electrons, the electron STWP can carry two different topologies, and host both meron and skyrmion topological textures in momentum space. We demonstrate the topological phase transitions and tunable skyrmion numbers by spectral geometry tuning. We also show the topologically robust propagation of the electron pulses and corresponding real-space skyrmionic expectation value textures encoded within each single electron wavefunction. Our results open a platform for topological free-electron wavepackets uses in sensing and information transfer.
summary: This paper explores free-electron Space-Time Wave Packets (STWPs) capable of carrying tunable topological textures, specifically Skyrmions and Merons. By constraining the momentum-space spectrum, the authors show how to create propagation-invariant wave packets. This work establishes a novel platform for using electron wave packets in topological sensing and information transfer.
main_problem: The paper investigates the properties of Space-Time Wave Packets (STWPs) for free electrons, focusing on their ability to carry and maintain tunable topological textures like Skyrmions and Merons.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that free-electron STWPs can be constructed to be propagation-invariant and host robust, real-space Skyrmionic expectation value textures by tuning the spectral geometry.
method: The study involves constraining the spatiotemporal spectrum of the electron wavefunction in momentum space and analyzing the resulting topology using spectral geometry.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using non-relativistic free-electron wave packets, analyzed in both momentum and real space. The topological structure is encoded in the local spin expectation value (SEV) of the electron spinor.
key_observables: Skyrmion number (Q), local spin expectation value (SEV), and the propagation invariance of the topological texture.
important_parameters: Group velocity ($v_g$), carrier wavenumber ($k_0$), and the spectral tilt angle ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to non-relativistic free-electrons, and the initial construction is noted to be a scalar construction lacking vector structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the construction of momentum space Skyrmions via closed spectral loops, the allowed parameter space for hosting Skyrmions/Merons, and the resulting robust real-space SEV textures.
paper_structure: The paper methodically constructs the STWP in momentum space, analyzes the topological constraints (Skyrmion vs. Meron), and then demonstrates the physical realization and robustness of these topological textures in real space.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from quantum optics (tunable wave packets) with condensed matter topology (Skyrmions) using matter waves (electrons), providing a platform for topological information transfer.
